ACCEPT. The written argument proves (1), the tree corollary, (2), and the stated sufficient-class consequence for the whole grid. I find no counterexample or substantive mathematical gap under the note’s vertex partition, feasibility condition, and residual-count definitions.The essential points are that every saturated tile inside the receiver has no matching endpoint, that parity uses all physical matching crossings, and that charges are always computed in the original configuration. Those facts make the regional ledger and subsequent addition valid without residual closure.1. The local pressured-tile argument is validThe feasibility condition alone excludes three or more selected corners: among any three corners of a square, one has two selected internal neighbors.The remaining cases give the asserted bound:Selected cornersConsequence of feasibility $t=0$  $b\ge t$  immediately. $t=1$ The selected corner’s two internal neighbors cannot both be occupied, so  $b\ge1$ . $t=2$ , adjacentEach selected corner already has its selected neighbor as an occupied neighbor. Both remaining corners must be blank. $t=2$ , diagonalA pressured face contains a selected corner. Its occupied external neighbor forces both internal neighbors to be blank.Thus a pressured tile satisfies  $b\ge t$ , and a pressured saturated tile has exactly two selected and two blank vertices, with no  $P$  endpoint.For the stronger cap statement, place the  $BB$  face at the bottom. The two remaining corners are adjacent, and each has an occupied external neighbor across one of the perpendicular pressured faces. If either remaining corner is  $T$ , the other must be  $B$ ; they cannot both be  $T$ . Their combined contribution to  $b-t$  is therefore nonnegative, and the cap contributes two. Hence
$$b-t\ge2.$$
No step constrains the direction of a matching edge or assumes that an external pressure witness is matched to a particular vertex. The argument uses its actual occupancy.One harmless wording clarification would be to replace “its partner must be  $B$ ” with “the other remaining corner must be  $B$ .” The proof concerns the adjacent corner, not a matching partner.2. Bent and branched geometry satisfies the required local hypothesesThe induced tile-adjacency condition is sufficient.A leaf has exactly one neighbor in  $R$ . Its opposite cap and both perpendicular faces are therefore exposed. The two perpendicular faces are pressured by hypothesis.Every nonleaf in a tree with at least two vertices has degree two or three. It consequently has at least one exposed face, and every such face is pressured under the stated assumptions.Each leaf is a distinct tile, so its two units of blank surplus belong to a distinct local summand.Bends, degree-three branches, and diagonal contacts do not change this argument. No straight continuation, preferred matching direction, or residual routing property is used.The requirement that both actual exterior neighbors exist is also correctly stated. A missing neighbor at the ambient rectangle boundary cannot supply pressure. Some shapes or placements may fail these hypotheses; the corollary is conditional on satisfying them.The claimed extension beyond trees is justified wherever the same local cap/pressure hypotheses hold. The proof uses the resulting pressured faces, rather than a tree-specific counting identity.3. The regional charge ledger is exactFor a deficient tile  $Q$ , write  $c_Q$  for its number of physical matching crossings. The matching endpoint partition and residual definition give
$$4=t_Q+b_Q+2h_Q+c_Q,\qquad d_Q=c_Q-s_Q.$$
Consequently,
$$\begin{aligned}
2\rho_Q
&=d_Q-2(2-t_Q-h_Q-s_Q)\\
&=c_Q+s_Q-4+2t_Q+2h_Q\\
&=t_Q-b_Q+s_Q.
\end{aligned}$$
This identity counts every physical matching direction correctly.Every tile of  $R$  has a pressured face, including the marked tiles. Therefore every saturated tile in  $R$  has  $t_Q=b_Q=2$ , contains no matching endpoint, and contributes zero to both  $\rho$  and  $t-b$ .It follows that every  $s_Q$  incidence from a deficient tile in  $R$  ends at a saturated tile outside  $R$ . Conversely, every edge counted by  $\sigma$  supplies exactly one such incidence. Hence
$$\sum_{\substack{Q\in R\\Q\text{ deficient}}}s_Q=\sigma,
\qquad
\boxed{\,2\rho(R)=t-b+\sigma\,}.$$
There is no missing residual boundary term. A residual matching edge leaving  $R$  remains included in its inside endpoint tile’s degree and hence in its boundary half-charge. The proof never restricts the residual graph to  $R$ .Capacity-two tilesThese are covered by the same identity. In particular,  $r_Q=2$  forces
$$t_Q=h_Q=s_Q=0,$$
so
$$2\rho_Q=-b_Q.$$
A capacity-two tile with four residual crossings has  $b_Q=0$  and charge zero. A marked capacity-two tile has at least its two cap blanks and therefore charge at most  $-1$ . Neither case receives a separate charge allowance for each residual passage.4. The parity correction and saturated-export allowance are correctSince  $M$  is a matching, its endpoints inside  $R$  consist of two endpoints for each internal matching edge and one for each physical crossing:
$$4|R_{\mathrm{tiles}}|=t+b+2\mu+j.$$
Thus
$$b-t\equiv j\pmod2.$$
The local inequalities sum to  $b-t\ge2L$ . Because  $2L$  is even,
$$b-t\ge2L+(j\bmod2).$$
Combining this with the exact regional ledger gives
$$2\rho(R)\le-2L+\sigma-(j\bmod2),$$
as claimed.Using physical  $j$  is essential: a saturated export is included in the matching endpoint partition even though it is excluded from the residual degree through  $d=c-s$ . The note correctly retains it.The normalization of the odd- $j$  allowance is also right. One saturated export contributes  $+\tfrac12$  to the regional charge formula. Odd  $j$  forces one additional unit of blank surplus, contributing  $-\tfrac12$ . Therefore
$$\sigma=1,\quad j\ \text{odd}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\rho(R)\le-L.$$
This establishes the conditional budget statement without asserting that every prescribed shape realizes that case.5. Aggregate compensation does not reuse the receiverLet
$$C=R\cup U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_k.$$
Tile disjointness and the use of charges from one fixed original configuration give exact additivity:
$$\rho(C)=\rho(R)+\sum_i\rho(U_i).$$
Hence
$$\rho(C)
\le
-L+\frac{\sigma-(j\bmod2)}2+L
=
\frac{\sigma-(j\bmod2)}2.$$
This remains valid when matching edges join two sources, join a source to the receiver, or join different cores. No boundary cancellation or residual-component decomposition is required.In particular, if an edge counted by  $\sigma$  ends in a saturated tile belonging to a source  $U_i$ , it remains counted in the receiver’s original  $\sigma$ . Taking the union does not authorize deleting that term or recomputing the constituent charges. The note’s full-configuration convention handles this correctly.The resources being added are also disjoint:Each marked tile contributes its own internal blank surplus.Each receiver appears once in its core.Sources and receiver are pairwise tile-disjoint.Distinct compensated cores are disjoint as whole tile sets.An external occupied vertex may support several feasibility implications. That does not duplicate a summed charge resource, because the surpluses lie inside different tiles.6. The whole-grid identity follows from the stated feasibilityThe final deduction can be checked directly, without taking the earlier ledger note on trust.Let  $D$  and  $S$  be the deficient and saturated tiles of the full rectangle. A saturated tile has at most one matching endpoint:Adjacent selected corners force both other corners blank.Diagonal selected corners permit at most one of the other corners to be occupied.Moreover, a physical matching edge cannot join two saturated tiles. If it did, both endpoint tiles would have diagonal selected corners. On the shared tile face, the two vertices other than the matching endpoints would both be selected. They are adjacent across that face, and each is already adjacent to its own tile’s matching endpoint. This violates the one-occupied-neighbor condition.Therefore every matching endpoint in a saturated tile is matched to a deficient tile. If  $p_S$  is the total number of matching endpoints in saturated tiles, then
$$\sum_{Q\in D}s_Q=p_S.$$
For every saturated tile,
$$t_Q-b_Q=|P\cap Q|,$$
and thus
$$\sum_{Q\in S}(t_Q-b_Q)=p_S.$$
Summing the deficient-tile ledger and using zero saturated charge now gives
$$\begin{aligned}
2\sum_Q\rho_Q
&=\sum_{Q\in D}(t_Q-b_Q+s_Q)\\
&=|T|-|B|-p_S+p_S\\
&=|T|-|B|.
\end{aligned}$$
The global matching partition is
$$mn=|T|+|B|+2|M|,$$
so
$$\boxed{\;
\sum_Q\rho_Q
=
|T|+|M|-\frac{mn}{2}
=q.
\;}$$
Consequently, pairwise tile-disjoint cores satisfying the compensation condition have nonpositive aggregate charge. If the remaining deficient tiles also have nonpositive aggregate charge, the remaining saturated tiles contribute zero and  $q\le0$  follows.The coefficient-one conclusion is therefore valid on the stated sufficient class. Its objective exceeds the coefficient- $5/6$  objective by exactly  $|M|/6$ , as asserted.No mathematical revision is required. This acceptance rests on the written general proof and the derivations above; the reported finite-control totals and Lean receipts are not needed for the verdict.
